build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: The player draws transit lines by clicking stations in sequence, connecting them with colored routes that trains automatically travel along. Score 0 if no line-drawing mechanic exists.
Passengers appear at stations with shape indicators showing their destination type, automatically board trains, and disembark at matching stations. Score 0 if no passenger system exists.
Stations that accumulate too many waiting passengers flash overcrowding warnings and eventually overflow, ending the game. Score 0 if stations have no capacity limit.
The player has limited resources (lines, carriages, tunnels) granted periodically, and must allocate them strategically as the city grows. Score 0 if resources are unlimited.
Lines can be rerouted at any time by the player, with trains smoothly transitioning to new paths and passengers re-routing accordingly. Score 0 if lines cannot be modified after placement.
New stations of different shapes (circle, triangle, square, diamond, star) appear over time, each representing a different destination type. Score 0 if only one station type exists.
At least 3 distinct map layouts with different geographic challenges: rivers requiring tunnels, islands, sprawling suburbs, or dense urban cores. Score 0 if only one map exists.
Resource grants offer meaningful choices: extra line, additional carriage for existing line, tunnel for river crossing, or interchange upgrade. Score 0 if no resource choices exist.
City growth escalates over time: more stations appear, passenger volume increases, and new station types demand longer routes and transfers. Score 0 if the city is static.
A run-end screen shows days survived, passengers delivered, network efficiency, and lines used. Score 0 if the game ends abruptly with no summary.
Normal startup shows a styled title screen with the game name, minimalist city-map imagery, and map selection. Score 0 if the game starts directly in gameplay or uses raw default UI.
The flow connects title to map selection to transit gameplay to resource-grant prompts to run-end without restarting the executable. Score 0 if major transitions are missing.
The map view clearly shows stations, lines, trains, passenger counts, and overcrowding warnings in readable non-overlapping regions. Score 0 if the player cannot determine network state.

Player actions produce visible feedback: line drawing shows the route forming, trains appear on new lines, overcrowding pulses warnings, passengers board visibly, and resource grants animate in. Score 0 if actions happen silently.

Art direction is coherent across title, city map, stations, trains, lines, and menus with a consistent minimalist transit-map palette and style. Score 0 if mostly default controls or mismatched placeholders dominate. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.
Stations, trains, passengers, geographic features, and UI elements use real illustrated art with a cohesive transit-design aesthetic. Score 0 if primary elements are unstyled rectangles.

Animation brings the network to life: trains glide along lines, passengers board and alight, stations pulse when crowded, new stations appear with fanfare, and lines draw smoothly. Score 0 if all elements are static.
HUD and UI panels use styled themed widgets with transit-map aesthetics, clean typography, or infographic-styled elements rather than raw HTML 引擎 defaults. Score 0 if all UI is default Label/Button.
